question: Refer to the exhibit. Cisco Fabric Services is enabled in the network. Which type of IP address is used by the Cisco Fabric Services protocol?
context:
SWB# ethanalyzer local interface mgmt brief limit-captured-frames 50
Capturing on mgmt0
1.130599 192.168.254.1 -> 192.168.254.13 TCP 60 29652 > ssh [ACK] Seq=1 Ack=53 Win=32449 Len=0
1.136261 00:8e:73:a2:41:0e -> Spanning-tree-(for-bridges)_00 STP 60 Conf. Root = 8192/10/ec:e1:a9:df:6c:80 Cost = 22 Port = 0x800e
1.373417 192.168.254.13 -> 192.168.254.1 SSH 106 Encrypted response packet len=52
3.270728 192.168.254.4 -> 239.255.70.83 UDP 166 Source port: cfs Destination port: cfs
theory: Cisco Fabric Services (CFS) is a peer-to-peer infrastructure Cisco MDS/Nexus NX-OS uses to automatically synchronize configuration (VSAN, zoning, device-alias, NTP, etc.) across every switch in a fabric, removing the need for manual per-switch configuration. When CFS distributes over IP (CFSoIP) rather than over Fibre Channel ISLs, it uses IPv4 multicast (239.255.70.83, UDP port 'cfs') so that any CFS-capable switch on the management network can dynamically discover its peers without static configuration, which is exactly what the ethanalyzer capture shows. This differs from CFS over FC, which piggybacks CFS frames as a proprietary SW_ILS over the fabric itself. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - Cisco Fabric Services (CFS))
